The earlier install went to `/tmp/.local/bin`, which isn't on this kernel's import path — so `pyproj` isn't importable. Let me install it properly into the running interpreter and verify.

```python
import subprocess, sys, importlib

print("interpreter:", sys.executable)
print("user site:", subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "site", "--user-site"],
                                   capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip())

r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "--user", "pyproj"],
                   capture_output=True, text=True)
print("pip rc:", r.returncode)
print((r.stderr or "")[-300:])

# make freshly installed user-site packages visible
import site
usp = site.getusersitepackages()
if usp not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, usp)
importlib.invalidate_caches()
print("user site on path:", usp in sys.path)

try:
    import pyproj
    print("pyproj OK, version:", pyproj.__version__)
except Exception as e:
    print("import still failing:", repr(e))
```
